findings.summary: The skip link targets a main element that cannot receive programmatic focus, so keyboard users may continue tabbing through the sidebar instead of bypassing it.
findings.fix: Add tabindex="-1" to the main element with id="main-content" so activating the skip link moves focus to the content.

findings.summary: Activating a mobile sidebar link returns focus to the menu button before navigating to a non-focusable section, leaving keyboard focus away from the newly displayed content.
findings.fix: Close the sidebar without returning focus when a navigation link is activated; make its destination focusable with tabindex="-1" and move focus to that destination after navigation. Keep returning focus to the button for Escape dismissal.
findings.evidence: The sidebar click handler calls setMenuOpen(false), which calls menuButton.focus().

findings.summary: Crossing the mobile breakpoint can hide the element that currently has focus without moving focus to a visible control.
findings.fix: When the breakpoint changes, check whether focus is inside the sidebar or on the menu button; before hiding that element, move focus to a visible, logical control in the new layout.
findings.evidence: The breakpoint handler closes the sidebar but does not relocate focus; CSS hides the sidebar on mobile and the menu button on desktop.

passed: Skip link is the first focusable element and is visually revealed on focus.
Links and buttons have a :focus-visible outline.
Mobile menu supports Escape dismissal and returns focus to its toggle.
No positive tabindex values were found in the scoped files.
notes: Automated keyboard testing could not reach the dashboard routes because they require sign-in; findings are based on the scoped template, CSS, and JavaScript.
